account:
It is noon on day 1, and I have reached home for my scheduled lunch after inspecting the mill. The mill stall held 73 hay bales at two emeralds each, but I still do not know who manages deliveries or how much stock is already committed. No town purchase has been authorized. My secretary has been helping with these enquiries and bringing the grain report.

There appears to be unusually large bread business underway. The secretary's report records that freight paid the baker 24 emeralds and supplied 72 wheat toward a private order of 200 loaves; another 528 wheat was needed, with hauling to be arranged today. I also overheard the baker saying the bakery chest was empty and seeking settlement and an innkeeper's promised thirty emeralds. I cannot yet tell whether that payment concerns the same order.

Several townsfolk have repeated news of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. One said the baker and neighbour were there, and that the baker carried a sack of bread. These are reports, not something I witnessed, and nobody has explained what actually changed. The baker was absent when I visited the bakery this morning. The repeated wording gives me little solid information about whether any bridge or port work is really planned.

There is also an appointment this evening at 18:00 for a great hall lighting inspection with the builder, added yesterday with my authorization; the secretary is to bring me into the hall. Taken together, the large bread order, the involvement of freight and possibly the innkeeper and neighbour, and the hall inspection might be preparations for a gathering, but that is only a suspicion. I have no confirmation of its purpose or of any connection between these matters. I should keep my appointments and ask those directly involved rather than treat the rumours as established facts.
